title: Sapphire Payments - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Initial discovery on Private VPC deployment for low-latency payments processing. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints, KMS integration, audit logs, and next steps including network diagram and security pack. Customer leaning toward Private (VPC) with dedicated capacity but needs clarification on cross-account peering and egress costs.
next_steps: Maria to send Private deployment whitepaper and security pack (incl. SOC2 docs)
Daniel to schedule technical deep-dive with platform team (deep-dive on peering and routing)
Customer to share network diagram and list of required regions and CIDR ranges
Exchange tentative POC timeline (2-4 weeks) and pricing options for Dedicated capacity
action_items: Maria Chen | Send private deployment whitepaper + SOC2 + KMS integration notes | 2026-03-06
Daniel Ortiz | Schedule technical deep-dive and invite infra engineers | 2026-03-08
Sapphire (Lina) | Share VPC CIDRs, preferred regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1) and proxy/NAT design | 2026-03-05
transcript:
[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're excited to talk through how Redwood can run in your private VPC for payments workloads. um, quick intros?
[00:10] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here, CTO at Sapphire. we handle transaction routing and reconciliation, high throughput, low latency is key.
[00:18] Lina Gomez: Lina, DevOps. I'm the one who'll likely pull the network config.
[00:21] Marcus Li: Marcus, security. will want to review audit and key management.
[00:25] Daniel Ortiz: Daniel from Redwood infra. I'll focus on the deep technical pieces like peering and endpoints.
[00:30] Maria Chen: Cool. quick agenda: confirm your constraints (regions, latency), walk through Private/VPC options (peering vs PrivateLink), discuss KMS and data residency, and outline next steps.
[00:44] Rajiv: Our big ones are: us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 DR, strict need for no egress to public internet for PII, and key material must be customer-managed if possible.
[00:55] Maria: Got it. when you say no egress to public, do you mean all traffic must stay in your VPC via PrivateLink or peering?
[01:03] Lina: Ideally private endpoints only. we don't want NAT gateways handling requests out.
[01:07] Daniel: ok, so two common patterns: cross-account VPC peering (or transit gateway) where Redwood's worker subnets are peered into your account, or PrivateLink/Interface endpoints where our control plane sits in Redwood but the data path traverses a private endpoint back to your VPC. each has tradeoffs.
[01:26] Marcus: For compliance we prefer the private endpoints model but worried about regional availability and connection limits.
[01:32] Daniel: fair. PrivateLink requires interface endpoints per AZ; there's ENI limits but we can size for your throughput. peering/transit gateway gives full layer-3 routing and may simplify DNS, but cross-account peering has routing and scale considerations and doesn't support transitive routing without TGW.
[01:48] Rajiv: What about latency differences? payments need sub-50ms tokenization calls.
[01:54] Daniel: We've measured PrivateLink in the mid single-digit ms within same AZ; across AZ add a bit. Peering with colocated workers in the same region also gives low latency. important: where the GPUs/serving nodes run — we can pin to specific AZs/regions in Private deployments.
[02:12] Maria: also worth calling out Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs Private. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with isolation but is still within Redwood's infra; Private means the control plane can be in Redwood but compute in your VPC (or fully private deployment).
[02:29] Lina: So with Private we can have the inference workers inside our account?
[02:33] Daniel: yes, two patterns: 1) VPC-hosted workers: you host the compute in your VPC (on-prem or cloud) and we provide an operator and control plane, or 2) cross-account peering where our workers are in an account we manage but peered to yours. both have different operational overheads.
[02:50] Marcus: Key management: can you integrate with our KMS? we can't give raw keys out.
[02:55] Daniel: we support customer-managed KMS through IAM roles and grant-less encryption patterns; we can also support HSM-backed keys if needed. we'll include the KMS flow diagram in the docs.
[03:05] Rajiv: How does S3 access work for model artifacts — we need to keep artifacts within our account.
[03:10] Daniel: we typically use cross-account roles or VPC endpoints to S3. for fully private deployments, models live in your S3 and workers have role-based access. we can avoid public S3 egress with VPC endpoints.
[03:22] Maria: any constraints around regions — we can run in most major regions but some accelerator types only available in select regions. what regions do you need?
[03:30] Rajiv: us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 for DR, maybe ap-southeast-1 later.
[03:36] Daniel: us-east-1 is fine for all instance types. eu-west-1 for DR is doable but check on some newest accelerators; we'll validate exact GPU SKU availability.
[03:46] Evan Park: On the networking side, what's the expected CIDR usage? we have a limited private IP pool.
[03:51] Daniel: we can operate with small CIDR allocations; for PrivateLink we mainly need ENI allocations per AZ and routes for the endpoint. for peering you'll need to ensure no overlapping CIDRs. we can also support proxy NAT designs if you prefer avoiding large IP allocations.
[04:07] Lina: Overlap is a problem for us — we have legacy VPCs. is there a workaround?
[04:11] Daniel: yes, options: use PrivateLink (no need to avoid CIDR overlap since it's endpoint-based), or use AWS Transit Gateway with NAT/route translation, or run the compute in your account so no peering required.
[04:24] Maria: question on billing/egress: if compute is in Redwood's account peered to yours, do you egress traffic and bill for it?
[04:31] Daniel: billing differs: Hosted has egress over public internet; Dedicated is still our network, but for Private deployments where workers are in your account, the egress stays in your VPC and you incur standard AWS egress only if data leaves region. we will include a cost breakdown.
[04:44] Marcus: Audit logs and access logging — we need API-level audit logs for all inference requests and admin actions, retained for 12 months.
[04:52] Daniel: Redwood can publish audit logs to your S3 or SIEM via Kinesis/Firehose; we support structured logs with token-level metadata. retention is configurable and we'll include sample log formats.
[05:06] Rajiv: SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO with role mapping.
[05:13] Maria: yes, we support SAML + SCIM and role-based permissions; we'll include admin onboarding docs.
[05:20] Lina: about certs and TLS — if PrivateLink is used, is mTLS supported?
[05:25] Daniel: mTLS is supported for customer-to-worker in the fully private pattern; for PrivateLink, TLS is standard and we can layer mTLS on top if you want.
[05:34] Maria: quick note, we'll attach our security questionnaire; please confirm you can fill it out.
[05:39] Marcus: we also need pen-test history and vulnerability scan cadence.
[05:42] Daniel: we have regular pentests and can share redacted reports under NDA; we'll put the schedule in the security pack.
[05:50] Rajiv: timeline: we'd like a pilot within 3 weeks if we can get network specifics and a small test cluster. possible?
[05:56] Maria: yes, typical POC 2-4 weeks. first step: share your CIDRs and regions, we'll propose architecture (PrivateLink vs peering) and an estimated cost for Dedicated vs Private.
[06:07] Evan: How about failover between regions — if us-east-1 has issues, can traffic failover to eu-west-1 without reconfig?
[06:14] Daniel: with active-active you need to plan routing and replication of KV caches; we have mechanisms for fallback but cross-region adds latency. for stateful sessions you might prefer sticky routing and fallback policies. export and prewarm caches in DR region for fast failover.
[06:30] Lina: we also run strict egress rules — can Redwood's control plane call back into our VPC for health checks or do we need to open inbound ports?
[06:38] Daniel: health checks can be initiated from workers inside your VPC; control plane callbacks can be via private endpoints. minimal inbound ports needed; we recommend mutual TLS and a small set of control-plane egress rules.
[06:53] Maria: ok i want to run through an example architecture: Customer-managed workers in your VPC, models stored in your S3 with role access, KMS CMKs for model decryption, PrivateLink for admin endpoints, audit logs to your S3. does that capture it?
[07:06] Rajiv: yes that sounds ideal.
[07:09] Marcus: What about software upgrades and patching of worker hosts?
[07:12] Daniel: if compute in your account, you control patching; we provide the operator and recommended AMIs/containers and automation playbooks. if compute in our account we handle upgrades under agreed maintenance windows.
[07:26] Maria: There was a question earlier about IP whitelisting for management APIs — we offer both token-based auth and IP restriction on control-plane endpoints.
[07:35] Evan: Are there any limits to concurrent requests or QPS for tokenization workloads?
[07:40] Daniel: depends on GPU SKU and model; we can provide throughput profiles. for high QPS, batching and auto-scaling policies help; Dedicated gives guaranteed throughput. we'll include a sample throughput table.
[07:53] Rajiv: Ok, security acceptance criteria: customer-managed keys, audit logs to our S3, SSO + SCIM, no public egress — is that something you can meet?
[08:04] Daniel: yes, all on the table. we'll document exact flows and any caveats (e.g., regional GPU availability).
[08:12] Maria: i'll summarize next steps at the end and confirm owners.
[08:16] Rajiv: quick question on IPSEC/VPN — we run site-to-cloud VPN to our colo. can Redwood be bridged over that?
[08:23] Daniel: yes, for fully private deployments you can run workers on-prem or in a colo with IPSEC to your VPC; we support hybrid with consistent routing.
[08:32] Lina: any concerns about cost of ENIs for PrivateLink? we run many endpoints already.
[08:37] Daniel: ENI costs are marginal compared to compute; the operational concern is quotas but we help plan the right number of endpoints per AZ and request increases if needed.
[08:49] Maria: we've also seen customers use a small fleet in each region for low-latency paths and a spillover region for cost savings.
[08:56] Marcus: one more — data residency. we can't allow EU customer data to leave eu-west-1 for processing.
[09:02] Daniel: that's enforceable by routing and model placement; we can pin workloads to region-level placement policies.
[09:09] Rajiv: ok sounds good. can you send a short network checklist we can use to prepare for the POC?
[09:14] Maria: yes — we'll include a network checklist (CIDRs, preferred regions, admin contact, S3 bucket ARNs, KMS key ARNs), plus a sample architecture diagram.
[09:26] Evan: if we provide the CIDRs, what's the fastest you can stand up a test cluster?
[09:31] Daniel: once we get CIDRs and IAM role details, we can provision a small cluster in 3-5 business days for POC.
[09:38] Maria: Great. i'll capture owners: Maria to send security pack and architecture options; Daniel to draft tech deep-dive agenda and throughput profile; Lina to share CIDRs and region list; Marcus to review security docs.
[09:53] Rajiv: Any blockers on your side?
[09:56] Daniel: none immediate. need to double-check GPU SKU availability for eu-west-1 and send that with the security pack.
[10:04] Maria: ok let's wrap with explicit next steps and timelines.
[10:08] (brief cross talk)
[10:12] Maria: Next steps recap: 1) Maria send security pack + SOC2 + KMS notes by 2026-03-06. 2) Lina share network diagram and CIDRs by 2026-03-05. 3) Daniel schedule technical deep-dive for week of 2026-03-08. 4) Redwood to propose POC architecture and estimate within 48h of receiving CIDRs.
[10:36] Rajiv: sounds good, thank you all.
[10:38] Maria: thanks everybody, we'll follow up via email and update the CRM.
[10:42] Meeting ends.
